voiceover: Your wedding isn't behind schedule. Here's what matters now. The Quiet List: what matters now, and what can wait. Zola's own planning guide says there is no required timeline. If you just got engaged this season, you're in good company. The Knot's data put December at the top for engagements. For a wedding a year or more away, three things matter now. Five can wait until after the holidays. And the one that feels urgent is on the wait list. One. Celebrate, and tell your closest people yourself before you post. Two. Pick a few date windows, and check holidays and conflicts. Three. Draft a rough budget and a rough guest list. Next in line is the venue. Every booking after it depends on it. Here's the part people skip: ask if you can bring your own vendors. Some venues restrict them, or charge an outside-vendor fee. Follow if you'd like tomorrow's: how to say adults only politely. Now the wait list. Zola's planning timeline counts months before the wedding. Your wedding party: month eleven, alongside the venue. Wait until budget, venue and style are settled. Attire: appointments start around month ten. Rushed buying can mean regret. Here's the one that feels urgent: save-the-dates. Six to eight months out, and earlier for destination weddings. Marriage license rules: month six on the checklist. Check your state and county: deadlines, fees and waiting periods. Invitations: order them in month four. One per household, plus ten to fifteen percent extra envelopes. Three now, five later. You're not behind. Save this for the next time a post makes you feel behind. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. Your wedding isn't behind schedule. Now you know what matters.

caption:
Just got engaged what to do first
Three things that matter now and five that can wait until after the holidays, with the month each one comes up on a planning checklist.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment:
The Quiet List: what matters now, and what can wait (for a wedding a year or more away).
Now: 1) celebrate and tell your closest people yourself 2) a few date windows 3) a rough budget and guest list
Next: the venue. Ask if you can bring your own vendors, and whether there is an outside-vendor fee.
Can wait (Zola's checklist counts months before the wedding): wedding party, month 11 / attire appointments, month 10 / save-the-dates, 6 to 8 months out / marriage license rules, month 6 / invitations, month 4
Norah is AI-generated.
comment_bait: Which task on the wait list felt most urgent to you?

sources.fact: No required timeline; celebrate first; tell your closest people in person or by phone before you post; shortlist date windows and check holidays and conflicts; draft a budget; location and date, then venue, then other vendors
sources.title: Just Engaged? Here's What To Do Next!

sources.fact: Wait a few weeks before asking anyone to be in the wedding; settle budget, venue and style first; do not buy attire until you know your budget; rushed purchases can lead to regret
sources.title: Just Engaged? Here's What To Do Next!

sources.fact: December is the most popular month to get engaged
sources.title: This Was the Most Popular Day to Get Engaged Last Year

sources.fact: Checklist by month before the wedding: 12+ months budget, rough guest list, venue research; month 11 venue and wedding party; month 10 attire appointments; month 8 save-the-dates (6 to 8 months out, earlier for destination); month 6 marriage-license rules; month 4 order invitations
sources.title: Your Ultimate Wedding Planning Checklist

sources.fact: Venue first: each booking narrows the next; some venues keep a preferred-vendor list or restrict florists, musicians and planners
sources.title: The 24 Questions to Ask a Wedding Venue BEFORE Booking

sources.fact: Some venues charge a fee to bring in outside vendors or caterers
